name: TinyZKP Example Receipt Workflows
summary: Concrete example workflows that map TinyZKP proof receipts to agent actions, API mutations, audit checkpoints, reserves, inventory, and long-trace sizing.

boundary.guidance: Examples are illustrative public statements. Generate a live receipt in the playground or API before using an example as evidence.

examples.title: Agent approval counter
examples.workflow: An agent supervisor tracks approved actions during a session and returns a receipt with the final checkpoint.
proves: The public approval counter advanced from 42 to 52 by the declared increments.
A downstream service can verify without replaying the agent transcript.
does_not_prove: That each real-world approval was correct.
That private approval details stayed hidden.

examples.title: Customer-visible API mutation
examples.workflow: A SaaS API attaches a receipt after a quota, seat, or balance mutation so the customer can verify the returned state.
proves: The public account checkpoint moved from 700 to 800 by the declared mutation batch.
The receipt can travel with the API response.
does_not_prove: That the quota policy was fair.
That hidden customer data was never processed elsewhere.

examples.title: Audit-log checkpoint
examples.workflow: An audit trail rolls many public event weights into a compact checkpoint that a reviewer can verify later.
proves: The published checkpoint advanced by the declared public increments.
An auditor can verify the arithmetic transition without replaying the full system.
does_not_prove: That every source event was legitimate.
That omitted events do not exist.

examples.title: Reserve aggregate update
examples.workflow: A finance workflow publishes a reserve or liability aggregate update and keeps the attestation boundary explicit.
proves: The public aggregate moved from 500 to 620 by the declared updates.
The receipt can sit beside a reserve or liability checkpoint.
does_not_prove: Custody, asset ownership, or external bank balances by itself.

examples.title: Inventory reconciliation
examples.workflow: An operations system turns a batch of inventory adjustments into a receipt-bearing reconciliation checkpoint.
proves: The published inventory accumulator advanced by the declared adjustment batch.
Another system can verify the checkpoint without database access.
does_not_prove: That the source ERP has no other records.

examples.title: Long trace sizing sample
examples.workflow: A large backfill starts with a small public statement, then moves to Compute once the trace length makes prover operations the bottleneck.
proves: The small sample statement is internally consistent.
The same workflow shape can be priced and reviewed for longer traces.
does_not_prove: That every future long trace fits latency limits.
That custom zkVM or zkML proving is generally available.

evaluation_use: Pick the example closest to the target workflow.
Generate the live receipt in the playground.
Copy the verifier result into the evaluation packet.
Replace the sample statement with real public parameters before production.
Use pilot review when the workflow is custom, private-input, on-chain, restricted-runtime, or long-trace sensitive.
